decision_conditions: The development must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date hereof.Reason: To comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, as amended.

All external facing materials, treatments and finishes shall be similar to those of the original building and maintained and retained thereafter. This applies unless differences are shown on the drawings we have approved. Reason: To ensure that the extension harmonises with the existing building and to ensure compliance with Policy 28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to the first occupation of the development hereby permitted, the car parking spaces, refuse and recycling storage enclosures, and secure cycle storage facilities shall be fully laid out, constructed, and installed on-site in strict accordance with the approved details shown on drawing no. 46CUL/006. All of these approved facilities shall thereafter be permanently retained and maintained for the lifetime of the development.Reason: To ensure that the development provides an adequate and satisfactory layout of off-street car parking, secure cycle storage, and waste management infrastructure. This is required to encourage sustainable modes of transport, prevent obstruction to the free flow of traffic, ensure adequate residential amenity, and safeguard the character and visual appearance of the local street scene in compliance with Policies 28, 29, 36, and 37 of the Sutton Local Plan (2018) and Policies T5, T6, and T6.1 of the London Plan (2021).

Prior to first occupancy of the development hereby permitted, a scheme for wildlife and nesting features shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. These will include but not limited to:- 2 x multi-chamber house sparrow terraces (facing adjacent vegetation where possible)- 2 x multi-chamber swift box (located under the eaves of the new extension)- 2 x starling box- Green roofs to proposed for refuse storage (e.g: products from Green Roof Shelters)Full details should be provided of the feature's location, height and distance from any external lighting (which if located too close, could prevent them from being successfully used), in plan and elevation views.Reason: To enhance the biodiversity value of the land in accordance with Policy 26 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to the commencement of development, a revised Energy Statement must be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing. The revised Energy Statement must incorporate:(i) updated 'as-designed' Standard Assessment Procedure (SAP) outputs based on current SAP 10.2 carbon factors which demonstrate how the proposed development will apply the Mayor's energy hierarchy (use less energy, supply energy efficiently and use renewable energy) to achieve at least a 35% reduction in carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions compared to the Part L 2021 baseline;(ii) further details of the proposed solar PV array, including roof plans; generating capacity and revised estimates of expected emissions savings. Reason: To comply with Policy 31 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

The development hereby approved shall be constructed in accordance with the approved Energy Statement as amended. Prior to occupation, 'as-built' Standard Assessment Procedure (SAP) outputs must be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing to demonstrate that the dwelling has achieved the targeted reduction in CO2 emissions. All of the approved measures must thereafter be retained for as long as the development is in existence. Reason: To comply with Policy 31 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

The development hereby approved shall be constructed in accordance with the approved Sustainable Drainage and Water Efficiency Strategy (V2) prepared by Freeflush Ltd and dated 31 January 2023. Prior to first occupation of the dwelling, written confirmation that the approved SuDS measures have been implemented as part of the development as built must be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing. All of the approved measures must thereafter be retained for as long as the development is in existence. roof plans Reason: To comply with Policy 31 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

The development must be carried out in accordance with the provisions of the approved Fire Strategy policy D12A.Reason: To ensure that the development incorporates the necessary fire safety measures in accordance with the Mayor's London Plan Policy D12.

Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (Amendment) (No. 2) (England) Order 2008 (or any Order amending or revoking and re-enacting that Order), planning permission shall be required in respect of development falling within Classes A and B of Part 1 of Schedule 2 of that Order.Reason: To ensure the retention of adequate outdoor amenity space for the future occupiers of the dwellings and in the interests of the character and appearance of the area in compliance with Policies 28 and 29 of the Sutton Local Plan.

No development shall commence (including any demolition and site clearance works) until a full Air Quality Neutral Assessment (AQNA), prepared in strict accordance with section 4.1.2 of the Air Quality Neutral London Planning Guidance, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Where the assessment identifies that the development fails to meet the relevant Transport Emissions Benchmark due to the proposed parking provision exceeding Policy T6.1 standards, full details of appropriate on-site mitigation, design adjustments, or offsetting measures shall be included within the submission. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details, and any required mitigation measures shall be fully implemented prior to the first occupation of the new dwelling and permanently retained thereafter.  Reason: To ensure that the development is air quality neutral and does not have an adverse impact on local air quality or the environment, in light of the proposed parking exceeding the maximum standards for a PTAL 2 zone in Outer London. This condition is required to be pre-commencement to ensure that necessary air quality benchmarks and mitigation strategies are fully integrated into the scheme prior to any physical works taking place, in accordance with Policy SI 1 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy 34 of the Sutton Local Plan (2018).
